ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two slanted straight lines labeled p and q, and the problem gives p ∥ q. An approximately vertical slanted line as a transversal passes through the upper line p at point B, point A is above B, and point D is on p and to the right of B; therefore ∠ABD is the angle formed by BA and BD, labeled in the figure as (3x - 60)°. The transversal continues to intersect the lower line q, and the exterior angle at the lower right is labeled (2x + 15)°. Reasoning: Because p ∥ q, these two labeled angles are on the same side of the transversal and are both exterior angles, so they are same-side exterior angles and are supplementary to each other. Therefore (3x - 60) + (2x + 15) = 180. Simplifying gives 5x - 45 = 180, 5x = 225, x = 45. Thus m∠ABD = 3x - 60 = 3(45) - 60 = 135 - 60 = 75.

raw_record.question_text: Refer to the figure at the right. Find the value of $m\angle ABD$ if $p \parallel q$.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify B as the intersection of transversal AF with the upper parallel line p, and D as a point on p to the right of B, so angle ABD is the angle labeled (3x - 60)°. Also read the lower exterior angle on the same right side of the transversal at line q as (2x + 15)°. From the text, use p ∥ q. Since these two labeled angles are same-side exterior angles formed by a transversal cutting parallel lines, they are supplementary: (3x - 60) + (2x + 15) = 180. Solve x = 45, then m∠ABD = 3x - 60 = 75.
